name: Deep Kaur
tagline: I turn ambiguous problems into shipped products, with AI and data at the core.
photoTooltip: hey, that's me. welcome to my portfolio
about:
I'm a product manager with 2 years of experience taking products from messy problem to production. At PCL, I led an AI-powered reporting suite from discovery to launch, adopted by 10,000+ users within 3 months and cutting manual reporting time by 80%. I also owned Oracle Cloud ERP and HCM delivery across 5+ enterprise clients.

I work from the user problem first: structured discovery, clear PRDs, and prioritization with frameworks like RICE, MoSCoW, and Value vs. Effort. I can also write the SQL, read the data, and brief senior stakeholders, so I can work closely with engineering and keep the roadmap realistic. I test new AI tools hands-on instead of just reading about them.

How I think about product: start with the problem and validate it before building. Prioritize with a framework, and know when to override it to protect core value. Measure adoption, not just delivery.

leadership.title: Leadership philosophy
leadership.body: I stay curious before I judge, and I'd rather be clear than clever. When things get messy, I stay calm, break the problem into small steps, and start with the one in front of me. I listen first and own my mistakes.

highlights: Strong foundation in computer science, algorithms, and software engineering.
Technical fluency in Python, SQL, and REST APIs that translated into product and data work.
Analytical, problem-solving approach later applied to product discovery and prioritization.

projects.title: Spotify: Product Lifecycle Analysis
projects.summary: Applied Atlassian's Product Lifecycle framework to Spotify's public disclosures to decide where the product stands and what a PM should investigate next.
projects.problem: Spotify has 777M users. Growth alone is no longer the question. The question is how to earn more without hurting the experience.
projects.approach: Segmented users and mapped the business model. Placed Spotify in the Maintenance and Optimization stage. Kept facts and my analysis clearly separate.
projects.insight: Prioritized monetizing highly engaged users. Chose to validate first instead of building.
projects.outcome: A validation plan with interviews, data analysis, and experiments. Success metric is Premium or add-on conversion. Guardrails are engagement and retention.

projects.title: LinkedIn: Job Seeker Experience
projects.summary: Outside-in analysis of the gap between applying and hearing back, with a first-hand data log, prioritized solution options, and a research plan.
projects.problem: Early-career candidates can't tell if a role is realistic. They also hear nothing after applying, so they have no signal on what to change.
projects.approach: Mapped the job seeker journey. Focused on two stages: evaluating fit and waiting. Logged 20 of my own applications. Only 2 showed any update beyond "Applied".
projects.insight: Scored six options with RICE. Recommended an MVP with a freshness signal and a status view with fallback states.
projects.outcome: A Figma wireframe, success metrics with guardrails, and a research plan. Interviews are still to come.

projects.title: Fair Share: Product Discovery and Prototyping
projects.summary: Competitive analysis, then validated the problem before building an interactive prototype.
projects.problem: Competitors deliberately ignored household fairness, leaving a clear market gap.
projects.approach: Competitive analysis, then validated the problem statement before building anything.
projects.insight: Prioritized features with RICE, then deliberately overrode the score to protect the product’s core value.

projects.title: Lineitem: B2B SaaS Spend Visibility PRD
projects.summary: Defined personas, a North Star metric, and an MVP from 14+ candidate features for B2B SaaS spend visibility.
projects.problem: B2B teams lack visibility and governance over SaaS spend, while buyers want autonomy.
projects.approach: Defined three personas and set a North Star metric that balances governance against buyer autonomy.
projects.insight: Prioritized an MVP from 14+ candidate features using MoSCoW and RICE, then mapped it to 6 epics and 9 user stories.
projects.outcome: Identified 8 cross-functional risks, each with a mitigation.

projects.title: From Presale to Packed House: Product Planning (Send Science)
projects.summary: Turned one feature idea into an epic with six shippable user stories, based on what stage the business was in.
projects.problem: Send Science's site is presale. No gym is open yet. Interested visitors can lose interest before opening day — that is where early excitement and money leak away.
projects.approach: Read the live site closely. Inferred the stage the business is in. Chose one epic: founding member conversion and engagement.
projects.insight: Skipped training features. No members exist yet to use them. Focused on keeping members engaged until the gym opens.
projects.outcome: One epic split into six stories, each with acceptance criteria. Stories cover signup, status page, progress updates, referrals, raffle tracking, and engagement nudges.
